target: NFR-PERF-001: p95 <= 200 ms over a 30-step navigation test
label: release build, USB cam nhung NOT_CHARGING (pin 80%), brightness manual 128, thermal status 0, 35.0C, refresh 60Hz

definitions.ms_to_frame: state change -> first frame after the image decoded. This is the one NFR-PERF-001 means by 'update the visible slice'.
definitions.ms_to_load: state change -> image decode reported. Kept so the decode/paint split is visible.
definitions.percentile: nearest-rank, no interpolation, no outlier removal

build_type: RELEASE — npx expo run:android --variant release; APK 68,815,824 bytes; flags=0x0 (FLAG_DEBUGGABLE not set)

conditions.power: USB connected, battery status 4 = NOT_CHARGING (level 80 -> 79). Charging had already stopped, so no charge-heating during the run.
conditions.refresh_note: Panel supports [90, 60]; 60 was active throughout. Frame budget 16.7 ms.

scope_limits: Fixture slices are 64x64. Real LGE MRI in-plane dimensions are NOT YET KNOWN — Spike D criterion A6 records the cohort shape distribution. This measurement is therefore a LOWER BOUND on slice-switch cost, not a demonstration at realistic data size, and A9 must be re-run once A6 reports the real dimensions.
A9 has a second half — 'no full-volume transfer per gesture' — which is NOT MEASURED here because the fixture is bundled locally and no network path exists yet. That half belongs with Spike E.
Single run of 30 steps. The criterion asks for a 30-step test, so the sample count is as specified, but one run does not characterise run-to-run variation.
Images are decoded from pre-encoded PNGs held in memory. A real viewer decoding from storage or network on demand will differ.
observation_for_A12: React Native Image applies bilinear filtering and exposes no nearest-neighbour option. On a 64x64 fixture scaled to ~1000 px the pixel grid is visibly smoothed, so displayed mask boundaries are smoother than the data. Not a factor in this timing measurement, but it matters for A5 and is a genuine mark against this candidate for a scientific viewer.
